key_insight: A deep-learning surrogate can replace expensive crystal plasticity simulations to optimize polycrystalline microstructures while balancing competing strength targets.
engineering_relevance: This enables practical, high-fidelity microstructure design for materials engineering by making multi-objective optimization of spall and yield strength computationally feasible.
method: Train a 3D U-Net to map 3D polycrystalline copper microstructures to full-field plate-impact velocity histories.
Couple the surrogate with stochastic microstructure generation and derivative-free optimization to search the design space.
Use a distribution-consistent reliability region (DCRR) based on MMD to track out-of-distribution risk during optimization.
evidence_signal: Across multiple optimization cases, CPFE validation showed less than 3% prediction error and the surrogate-driven workflow cut cumulative evaluation time by about four orders of magnitude.
watch_item: Performance depends on staying within the training-data distribution, so surrogate reliability must be monitored carefully when exploring new microstructure regimes.
paper_title: Deep learning driven framework for optimization of polycrystalline microstructures under competing strength requirements
